item.title: Jordan Clarkson toasts Knicks culture after win over Bucks
item.description: © Lucas Boland-Imagn Images Jordan Clarkson toasts Knicks culture after win over Bucks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The transformation Jordan Clarkson has undergone in his career is quite breathtaking. Of course, the physical changes are the most apparent. He changed up his hair and he has both sleeves fully tatted up. But Clarkson has become the quintessential role player, embracing his part to play to help this New York Knicks team achieve their goals. On Tuesday, Clarkson played just 11 minutes and scored two points on 1-of-5 shooting from the field in a 117-85 win for the Knicks over the Milwaukee Bucks. But his words after the game show that he is all-in on the culture of this team and is willing to do whatever it takes to get his team the victory. “That’s just our culture here. No matter if it’s one minute, 30 seconds, 30 minutes during the game. That’s what we focus on. That’s what Mike has preached to us since he’s got here and that’s just a big thing all of us hold our hat on,” Clarkson said after the game, via SNY Knicks on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "That's just our culture here- no matter if it's one minute, 30 seconds, 30 minutes during the game. That's what we focus on." Jordan Clarkson talks about focusing on the little things to help the Knicks win: pic.twitter.com/gg1VSjglPK — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) November 11, 2026 Clarkson’s role has been fluctuating over the past year or so, and he’s no longer the Sixth Man of the Year-caliber player he was in years past. Nonetheless, what makes the 34-year-old guard a valuable player for the Knicks despite his decline has been his ability to just stay ready and make the most of his minutes, however many he ends up playing. Make no mistake about it, Clarkson can still get buckets when called upon. But the Knicks have scarcely needed him to, and yet he’s well content just doing whatever the coaching staff tells him to, which is a testament of the kind of respect the team’s coaching staff commands. Clarkson is currently averaging just 6.0 points per game, which would be the lowest of his career. But if the Knicks keep on winning games, that should be all that matters to the 34-year-old NBA champion . item.title: Padres sign ex-Astros pitcher to major league deal with 2028 option
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Padres sign ex-Astros pitcher to major league deal with 2028 option appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Diego Padres have added some pitching depth early in the offseason , agreeing to a deal with former Houston Astros right-hander Ryan Weiss. Weiss is signing a one-year major league contract with the Padres that includes an option for 2028, according to Jesse Rogers . The financial terms of the deal were not immediately disclosed. Rogers noted that Weiss drew interest from around the league and also had a chance to return to the KBO, where he pitched in 2025, before ultimately getting a deal done with San Diego. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The signing gives Weiss another shot at proving himself in the majors after a rough 2026 campaign in Houston . The 29-year-old made nine appearances for the Astros, including two starts, going 0-3 with a 7.62 ERA and a 2.12 WHIP over 26 innings. He did show some swing-and-miss stuff, though, striking out 30 batters in that span. Weiss’ struggles in Houston came after a breakout stint overseas that put him back on the radar of MLB teams. Pitching for the Hanwha Eagles, he posted a 3.16 ERA and racked up 305 strikeouts across 270 1/3 innings over two seasons in South Korea. That performance earned him a major league deal with the Astros last offseason . Houston guaranteed him $2.6 million for 2026, with a club option for 2027 and incentives that could have pushed the total value past $10 million. Originally a fourth-round pick by the Arizona Diamondbacks in the 2018 MLB Draft, Weiss will now get a fresh start in San Diego. The Padres are hoping a change of scenery can help Weiss rediscover the form that made him one of the KBO’s top arms. At the very least, he gives San Diego a versatile option who can fill in both as a starter and out of the bullpen . With an option for 2028 attached to the deal, the Padres also have some flexibility if Weiss pans out. Well, this was a disappointing day for the Cincinnati Bengals . There was some hope that, with all of the activity around the AFC during the trade deadline, the team was going to do something as well. And they did! They executed a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles that seemed good on paper… up until Cincinnati reneged on the deal all of a sudden. Now, the Bengals are left in a weird position after the trade deadline. What was their biggest mistake this trade deadline? Bengals’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline: Not checking their compensatory picks properly The biggest mistake that the Bengals made at the trade deadline isn’t necessarily their decision to back out of the Arnold Ebiketie trade. It’s not the fact that they didn’t swing for the fences for a star running back or more defensive pieces. The fact that they didn’t do anything at all at the trade deadline isn’t the biggest mistake they made today. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) No, their biggest mistake was agreeing on the Ebiketie trade without seemingly doing their research. Cincinnati’s whole reason for backing out of the Ebiketie trade with the Philadelphia Eagles was because they did not know that they would lose a compensatory pick in the process. The Bengals were going to lose the compensatory pick they got when Trey Hendrickson left in free agency this season. That decision alone is a mistake already: why is this win-now team this worried about a compensatory pick? What’s truly baffling, though, is the fact that the Bengals did not know this beforehand. Yes, the compensatory draft pick system is needlessly convoluted and gives every fan a headache. There’s a lot of math and weird cancellations that go into the process. It’s understandable for your average Joe to not have a good grip on this system. The Bengals aren’t your average Joe. They are an NFL organization with the tools to hire people knowledgeable about this topic. You’d expect a front office to have someone on hand to know about this. item.title: Robert Griffin III urges fans not to count out Ohio State football
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Robert Griffin III urges fans not to count out Ohio State football appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Robert Griffin III weighed in on Ohio State football ’s outlook Tuesday night after the Buckeyes dropped eight spots in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. Ohio State landed at No. 20 after opening at No. 12. The slide followed Saturday’s 41-28 home loss to the Oregon Ducks, which left coach Ryan Day ’s team at 6-3 overall and 4-2 in Big Ten play. The ranking marked a program low in the CFP era. Ohio State’s previous lowest placement was No. 16 in the committee’s inaugural rankings in October 2014. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Griffin, the 2011 Heisman Trophy winner at Baylor, addressed the Buckeyes’ outlook Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter, with a brief message as they prepare for their final three regular-season games. “Don’t count out Ohio State yet.” The Buckeyes face uncertainty at quarterback as they look to rebound from consecutive losses. Julian Sayin remains out indefinitely after suffering a throwing-arm injury during Ohio State’s October 17 win at Indiana. Day has described a regular-season return as doubtful. Freshman Luke Fahey has started the losses to USC and Oregon. Against the Ducks, he completed 36 of 50 passes for 360 yards and two touchdowns, while Jeremiah Smith finished with seven catches for 133 yards and a score. All three teams that have beaten Ohio State remain in the committee’s rankings. Texas is sixth, Oregon is 16th, and USC is 18th. The Buckeyes host Northwestern on November 14 at noon ET/9 a.m. PT on FOX before visiting Nebraska on November 21. They close the regular season against Michigan at home on November 28. Ohio State currently remains outside the projected playoff field, with three regular-season games left to improve its resume before the selection committee determines which teams reach the postseason. item.title: How Bradley Braves basketball lost road opener at Davidson, prep for Coppin State duel next
item.description: DAVIDSON, N.C. — The Bradley Braves had a cold-shooting first half and could not make up a deficit in the second half against the Davidson College Wildcats on Tuesday. The Braves lost their season road opener, 62-45, before 2,036 at Belk Arena in Davidson , N.C. The Braves slipped to 1-2 on the season, while Davidson moved to 3-0. Bradley, an 11.5-point underdog heading into the game, chipped a deficit down to four points in the second half before fading. The game marked the opening of a three-game trip this week, which continues with matchups against Coppin State and George Mason on Thursday and Saturday, respectively, in the Showdown in St. Pete at St. Petersburg, Fla. The Braves scored 20 points in the first half at Davidson, shot 26.9% from the field and 1 of 10 from 3-point range. In the home opener against Pacific last weekend, Bradley scored 19 points in the first half, shot 21.4% from the field and 3 of 13 from 3-point range. "Obviously our offense is really struggling right now," Bradley head coach Brian Wardle said. "We tweaked some things after our last game ... it's gonna take a little time, so we're going to have some growing pains with it, play more five-out, more of a motion. That's what the players felt comfortable with, so I'm willing to adjust. But just careless passing, decision making, foul trouble hurt us in the first half." "We need to rise above it" Veteran guard/forward Timoty van der Knaap made his regular-season debut, returning from a foot injury and jumping into the starting lineup. He struggled to an 0 of 11 shooting night. Bradley continues to be without its starting guard tandem in Dietrich Richardson and Georgi Gerganov, the latter out for the season with a major knee injury suffered in the summer. Richardson is fighting a foot injury, and missed his second straight game. "We have to get a specialist to look at Dietrich," Wardle said. "We've had an X-ray and an MRI, and so he's out this week, and we'll look at next week and figuring out what the next step is with him. "It's unfortunate, because we miss his playmaking, and miss his paint touch ability and his ability to get to the rim. But you know, that's part of the season, next man up. There's no excuses. We are not gonna fall victims to our consequences at all. We need to rise above it and figure this out." What the Braves said ◾ Bradley head coach Brian Wardle: "Shot making ... we gotta find some guys that can make some shots and string together some buckets for us so that we can take some pressure off our defense. It's going to take a little time, and that's all I can say. We have a ton of new people." ◾ Wardle, on his rebuilt roster: "Everyone is trying to take a step up in roles. It's big pressure and big adjustment for a lot of these guys. They weren't the No. 1 or No. 2 guys last year. Some of them are the three, four, five or six guys on their (previous) team. So we're trying to get them, you know, who's gonna be our No. 1 and No. 2? I don't know yet." ◾

item.title: Cincinnati Reds hire Anthony Iapoce as assistant hitting coach
item.description: LAS VEGAS – The Cincinnati Reds rounded out their coaching staff this week with the hiring of veteran hitting coach Anthony Iapoce as the new assistant hitting coach.The move creates a reunion of Iapoce and Reds head hitting coach Chris Valaika.Valaika was an assistant to Iapoce in their only previous year coaching together, 2021 with the Chicago Cubs .Iapoce most recently worked as the Astros ’ assistant hitting coach last season after two seasons as the Tigers’ first base coach. The 1994 draft pick of the Milwaukee Brewers spent nince seasons as a minor-league outfielder, reaching Triple-A in both the Brewers and Marlins system, and producing a career .345 on-base percentage with 168 stolen bases.The move comes less than a week after the Reds hired Cleveland Guardians assistant pitching coach Joe Torres as their new head pitching coach . Team president Nick Krall said the team is still working through specific roles for some of staff, including the two other pitching coaches under Torres: Matt Tracy and Oscar Marin. item.title: Kentucky Basketball and Mark Pope continue to struggle under the bright lights
item.description: Kentucky Basketball fell to the Kansas Jayhawks on Tuesday night in the State Farm Champions Classic, 89-69. Aside from Zoom Diallo, the No. 24 Wildcats never seemed to be in rhythm due to foul trouble and an offensive game plan that fell short of making much sense. Diallo (24 points) was the only real source of offense for Kentucky with Malachi Moreno battling early foul trouble just minutes into the game and Milan Momcilovic being a ghost for most of the game. Sadly, the dud by head coach Mark Pope and the Wildcats almost felt expected. After all, between former HC John Calipari and Pope, Kentucky is now 2-8 in their last 10 Champions Classic appearances with their only two victories coming in a narrow win over Duke in 2024 and a similar outcome over Michigan State in 2019. They’re also 1-6 in their last seven matchups in the event. Meanwhile, Tuesday night was the Cats’ worst loss in the Champions Classic since 2018. Even more tragic is that this is something that has happened to Kentucky regularly under Pope, whose teams continued to get manhandled far too often by good competition. Kentucky has trailed by 17 or more in their last 4 games vs Top 25 competition. — Steven Peake (@StevenPeakeKSR) November 11, 2026 View Link It has to be frustrating for Big Blue Nation to see their teams struggle so much year after year. All night long, Dan Shulman and Jay Bilas commented on how sluggish Kentucky’s offense looked compared to Kansas’s ball movement, while also pointing out the astonishing difference in fast-break points, steals, and offensive rebounds — all fueled by playing with more intensity. Kentucky’s deflating loss will leave their fans with more questions than answers, and they won’t play another top-25 team until No. 6 Virginia in early December. That same Cavaliers team beat John Calipari’s Arkansas so bad they were leading by 27 at one point in the 91-72 win over the Razorbacks. The Wildcats will next host North Arizona on Friday at Rupp Arena with tip-off scheduled for 7 PM ET.

item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. But perhaps this led to Brown being too deep in his own head that he wasn’t able to find his rhythm on the offensive end after getting into foul trouble. The 76ers will need him to play better, and now, he has two months to simmer down as he awaits another opportunity to face the Celtics — this time at his former home at TD Garden. item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals should be riding high this week. They're 6-2 and coming off their most impressive win of the season . The national TV loudmouths started the week raving about how Joe Burrow and the Bengals may just be a Super Bowl contender. It looked like the positive momentum was going to continue on Nov. 10, when it was reported early in the day that the Bengals had made a trade for a veteran pass rusher ahead of the NFL's late-afternoon trade deadline. Somehow, though, the Bengals emerged from the deadline a national embarrassment. Turns out, the Bengals didn't make a trade. And then in typical fashion, they refused to answer questions and take public responsibility for what happened. The Bengals were left with a public-relations mess that the NFL's smallest player personnel department didn't do its homework before agreeing to acquire Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles. Cincinnati had to rescind it, but offered no explanations. The organization declined multiple requests from The Enquirer to answer questions or provide a public statement. It gets worse for the Bengals, a franchise that was supposedly operating like this is a championship-or-bust season. Actual Super Bowl contenders went out and made big trades to improve their teams, including AFC standard-bearers Buffalo and Jacksonville. The Bengals have failed to put themselves in the same conversation with the Bills and Jaguars, who beat Cincinnati last month. The Bengals needed help on a defense that continues its yearslong struggle to stop the run and cover the middle of the field. The Bengals got nothing. Instead, they're getting laughed at − and they deserve it. The front office unintentionally pulled back the curtain and showed everyone they're still the Bungles. Remember us! item.title: Blue Jays GM Ross Atkins Names Surprising CF Option
item.description: Ross Atkins Blue Jays Getty Toronto Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins named a surprising option for the team’s vacancy in center field for next season. The Blue Jays traded former center fielder Daulton Varsho to the Houston Astros at this year’s trade deadline. Though Varsho is a free agent, he won’t be coming back to Toronto, so the team is looking at other options for the CF position. While a trade or free-agent pickup can’t be ruled out, it appears the team will stick in-house to fill the void, with Atkins naming a surprising option to play the position next year. Addison Barger Could Play CF for Blue Jays Speaking to Blue Jays reporters in Las Vegas, Atkins mentioned that Brett Bateman and Nathan Lukes could both play center field for Toronto next year, two names that aren’t surprising given they are two of the team’s best defensive outfielders. But he also named Addison Barger as a third option to play CF, which is a big surprise given Barger is more of a corner outfielder and third baseman, and also because he missed most of last season due to injuries . Still, it looks like the Blue Jays might give Barger the chance to get into the CF mix next year. “Interesting note from Ross Atkins when asked about the Blue Jays’ CF depth chart. Along with Brett Bateman & Nathan Lukes, he named Addison Barger as an option.” Interesting note from Ross Atkins when asked about the Blue Jays' CF depth chart. Along with Brett Bateman & Nathan Lukes, he named Addison Barger as an option. — Ben Nicholson-Smith (@bnicholsonsmith) November 10, 2026 Addison Barger Blue Jays Career The Blue Jays drafted Barger in the sixth round of the 2018 MLB Draft. The 26-year-old Washington native then made his MLB debut for Toronto in 2024 before having a breakout season in 2025 when he hit 21 home runs as the Blue Jays made it all the way to the World Series. That included Barger hitting a pinch-hit grand slam in Game 1 of the 2025 World Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers , a first in MLB history. Unfortunately, Barger was banged up for most of 2026, playing in just 9 games for the team and having only 1 hit. In his MLB career, Barger has played in 99 games in the outfield, but they have come only in right field and in left field, so moving to center field would be a big change for Barger, who has also played in 127 games at third base for Toronto. Though Barger has a rocket arm, his lack of speed and range makes him a better option for the corners for Toronto, but it sounds like he’ll get a chance to at least try out at CF for the Blue Jays next season. item.title: Josh Hart injury update gives Knicks reason for optimism as Mike Brown reveals latest
item.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images The New York Knicks have received an encouraging update on Josh Hart’s ankle injury after head coach Mike Brown suggested the guard was close to returning before their clash with the Milwaukee Bucks. Hart missed his third consecutive game against Milwaukee, having previously sat out matchups with the Chicago Bulls and Cleveland Cavaliers because of an ankle problem. However, illness was the only thing keeping him out of the latest contest. The 31-year-old has been an important contributor for New York this season, averaging 8.6 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.9 assists and a team-high 2.1 steals. Mike Brown suggests Josh Hart would have played against the Milwaukee Bucks without illness Speaking before the game, Brown indicated Hart’s ankle was no longer preventing him from taking the court. “From what they’ve told me, correct me if I’m wrong, if he was not sick, he would play tonight,” Brown said, in a video posted by SNY. That will be welcome news for the Knicks, who have been looking to maintain their momentum during Hart’s absence. Landry Shamet has stepped in admirably, but Hart offers a different level of versatility with his work across the floor. His contribution is not limited to scoring. Hart regularly sets screens, makes defensive rotations, chases loose balls and creates opportunities for teammates with his passing. There has also been some discussion about fatigue within the Knicks squad, with Hart acknowledging that the physical demands of the season were already becoming noticeable. “Sometimes it takes us a little longer to get into the game. Whether that’s the flow, whether that’s fatigue,” Hart said. “We all feel the fatigue. We’ve got to fight through it. It’s six games in. We’ve got to find a way to get our bodies ready to play. Mentally, we’re there. We’ve got to find it physically.” New York went on to secure a convincing 117-85 victory over Milwaukee, improving its record to 6-4. Jalen Brunson led the way with 23 points, while Karl-Anthony Towns added 21 points and 16 rebounds. OG Anunoby also contributed 19 points as the Knicks controlled the contest. Hart’s return would give Brown another valuable option as New York looks to build on the win.
